ingles.titulo: Did You Know the Sargasso Sea Hides a Millennial Mystery?
ingles.descripcion: Did you know that in the Atlantic there is a borderless sea covered in floating seaweed? It stretches from 20°‑35° N to 40°‑70° W, 1,100 km wide and 3,200 km long. The water can be clear up to 60 meters, a true underwater mirror. The Portuguese called it Sargasso; in 1492 a captain feared being trapped by lack of wind. The Dana expedition (1920‑1922) discovered that the European eel reproduces there. Imagine hundreds of eggs floating in the blue mist of the ocean.
